ety.text: From азо́т (azót) + -о- (-o-) + содержа́щий (soderžáščij), a calque of German stickstoffhaltig. First attested in 1859.
From алма́з (almáz) + -о- (-o-) + носи́ть (nosítʹ) + -ный (-nyj). Compare Ukrainian алмазоно́сний (almazonósnyj).

ety.text: Ostensibly from вина́ (viná) + -ова́тый (-ovátyj), but since the suffix is normally attached to adjectives and not nouns, may instead represent a dissimilation of вино́вный (vinóvnyj) + -ова́тый (-ovátyj). Replaced ви́нный (vínnyj) in the 19th century due to homonymy.
Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic въсточьнъ (vŭstočĭnŭ). By surface analysis, восто́к (vostók) + -ный (-nyj).
